enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1059 AM MST Mon Nov 9 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 936 AM MST Mon Nov 9 2026

 - Dry conditions and light winds persist through the work week.
   Patchy fog develops Tuesday morning.

 - Next potential system arrives late this week which could bring
   more rain chances. 

 - Near-normal temperatures through the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 936 AM MST Mon Nov 9 2026

Lower clouds linger along the Int'l border today associated with 
the low pressure over W TX. Very little chance of rain for 
Hudspeth County this afternoon as drier air filters in from the 
north and erodes much of the cloud cover. The low slides to the 
east by Tue and opens up into a shortwave, taking most of the
moisture with it. Areas of low clouds/fog may redevelop Tue AM 
under the clearing skies and calm winds. Otherwise, mainly clear
with light winds for Tue as upper ridging moves in from the west.

The ridge becomes more amplified Wed/Thu and shifts overhead, 
keeping us mainly clear with generally light winds. A weak 
backdoor front arrives on Wed, bringing modestly breezy N-NE winds
that day. 

A shortwave trough pushes in from the Pacific by Sat associated 
with a negatively tilted longwave. Increasing clouds are forecast 
for Fri ahead of the disturbance, followed by a low chance of rain
Fri night-Sat. Global models and ensembles have sped up the
system, so Sun now looks dry. Mostly light rain showers are
forecast with minimal threat of flash flooding. A few
thunderstorms can't be ruled out as the LREF shows modest
instability Fri evening along with PVA. Most likely rain amounts
are <0.1" as southern areas are favored to see precip. Snow levels
will be high (9-10kft) during the event, so accumulations are not
expected, although a rain/snow mix can be seen on the highest
elevations through Sat. The shortwave departs to the east on Sun,
leaving us with another ridge of high pressure to end the period.
Temperatures hold near normal, cooling slightly for the weekend.

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 936 AM MST Mon Nov 9 2026

Low clouds hang around this afternoon, favoring KELP with MVFR
CIGs at 025-030. Cloud bases rise slightly by the evening then 
thinning out around 0z. Low clouds/fog may develop early Tue AM, 
most likely near KDMN. Confidence is too low for any mention of 
fog or mist for this TAF cycle. Any fog mixes out around mid- 
morning. Winds AOB 6kts.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 936 AM MST Mon Nov 9 2026

No fire weather concerns are forecast through the week. Light
winds for the rest of today with high RHs outside of the Gila.
Lingering low clouds down south this afternoon with areas of fog
developing overnight. Trending drier into midweek with mainly
clear skies as RHs remain above critical thresholds. Light winds
continue through midweek, although a weak front brings some
breeziness from the N-NE on Wed. Winds of 10-15 mph with gusts to
25 mph are forecast for Wed in the Sacs. No chance of rain until 
Fri night-Sat when a wx system brings low rain chances. Temps will
be near normal.

Min RHs range from 40-60% on Tue for S and E areas, 20-40% NW;
then 20-45% area-wide through Fri. Vent rates will be mostly poor
through Thu.
